newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER'S BLUNDER HELPS ARGENTINA BEAT COLOMBIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER'S BLUNDER HELPS ARGENTINA BEAT COLOMBIA.

text.p: A bizarre goalkeeping blunder allowed Argentina to beat Colombia 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday and wreak revenge for one of the biggest humiliations in their soccer history.
Colombian goalkeeper Farid Mondragon committed an astonishing error of judgment in the ninth minute when he thought a 25-metre shot by Claudio Lopez was going out of play.

He allowed the ball to pass him but to his horror, instead of going out, it trickled into the Colombian net to hand Colombia their first home defeat in a World Cup qualifier since 1985 -- when they also lost to Argentina.
It was a thoroughly frustrating match for Colombia, who began the day as outright leaders of the South American World Cup qualifiers with a proud unbeaten record.

They failed to capitalise on playing the entire second half with a one-man advantage, after Argentina's Eduardo Berizzo was sent off before halftime for a foul on Rene Valenciano, and also missed a penalty in the 54th minute.

Argentina, who have suffered some disappointing results in the qualifiers, produced one of their best performances since Daniel Passarella took over following the 1994 World Cup as they moved into third place in the nine-team group.

They also went a long way to wiping out memories of their last World Cup qualifier with Colombia in 1993, when they were beaten 5-0 in Buenos Aires -- one of the darkest moments Argentine soccer has ever suffered.

Ironically, Mondragon, who plays his club soccer in Argentina with Independiente, has established a reputation for being a solid goalkeeper in sharp contrast to his predecessor, the eccentric but error-prone Rene Higuita.
Lopez's early goal unsettled Colombia and Argentina missed two gilt-edged chances to increase their lead before halftime.

Colombia, with captain Carlos Valderrama producing another slick display which belied his 35 years, settled down after the interval and put the visitors under more pressure in an exciting and dramatic game.
The Colombian midfielder was hugely creative but, with striker Faustino Asprilla suffering an off-day, they were unable to convert numerous promising attacks into goals.
Mauricio Serna missed the best chance in the 54th minute when he fired a penalty wide of the goal after Asprilla was fouled by Hernan Diaz.

Another chance went begging in injury time when Antony Avila, whose over-individualistic play spoilt several attacks, completely mistimed a header and failed to connect with a cross in front of the Argentine goal.

Both countries came to a near standstill during the match, with shops and offices shutting, and thousands of Argentines poured onto the streets of Buenos Aires to celebrate when the final whistle went.

Colombia - Farid Mondragon, Wilmer Cabrera, Jorge Bermudez, Alexis Mendoza, Hugo Galeano (Antony de Avila), Leonel Alvarez, (Victor Pacheco), Mauricio Serna, Carlos Valderrama, Freddy Rincon, Ivan Rene Valenciano, Faustino Asprilla.

Argentina - Ignacio Gonzalez; Hernan Diaz, Roberto Sensini, Eduardo Berizzo, Pablo Paz, Diego Simeone, Gustavo Zapata, Juan Veron, Ariel Ortega, Hernan Crespo (Nelson Vivas), Claudio Lopez (Juan Pablo Sorin).
